cited_evidence: Behavioural criterion: "Select all qualifying or fallback demand records and preserve record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight."
Top-level input example: record_id n06-r01 has demand_score 9 and source_weight 5.
Job_2 input needs example: record_id n06-r01 has demand_score 9 and source_weight 9, showing source_weight was changed before downstream processing.
Upstream select_demand source appends {'source_weight': row.get('demand_score', 0)} instead of preserving row.get('source_weight', ...).
Handoffs show exact producer/consumer hashes for needs and evidence_sources, so job_2 received the upstream artifacts as handed off.
initial_receipt.explanation: The two-job execution contains an upstream provenance fault. The required behavior says selected demand records must preserve source_weight, but job_1's select_demand constructs output records with source_weight taken from demand_score. This changes the top-level corpus source weights before the exact handoff to job_2. Job_2 then consumes the handed-off needs/evidence_sources exactly and ranks consistently from those inputs, so the responsible job is the upstream job and the responsible function is select_demand.
